title: osf doctor: read-only setup report
summary: Adds a new `osf doctor` subcommand that inspects the repository and machine and prints a read-only report of six checks — osf version pin, settings load, enabled agents and their credentials, agent binaries, git hooks, and container image. The command reuses existing modules (config, agents, githooks, reviewers) rather than adding new machinery, supports text or JSON output and a single-check filter, and exits non-zero when any check fails.

nodes.label: osf main
nodes.subtitle: Command::Doctor dispatch
nodes.summary: Adds the Doctor variant to the clap Command enum, the DoctorArgs/DoctorFormat argument structs, and doctor_cmd, which resolves the repo root, builds the report, filters it, prints text or JSON, and maps a failing check to exit code 1.

nodes.label: doctor::report
nodes.subtitle: fn report(root, config_file) -> Vec<Check>
nodes.summary: Assembles the six checks in fixed report order: osf, settings, agents, agent-binaries, hooks, container. Pure orchestration — each check is a small function below it.

nodes.label: doctor::keep
nodes.subtitle: fn keep(checks, wanted) -> Result<Vec<Check>, String>
nodes.summary: Filters the report down to one named check, or errors with the list of valid names when the caller passes an unknown one. Backs the --check flag and the exit-code-2 usage error.

nodes.label: Check / Status
nodes.subtitle: name, status, detail, fix
nodes.summary: The serialisable report line: a name, a Status (ok/warn/fail/unknown), a human detail string, and an optional fix hint. Status::as_str supplies the text-report word.

nodes.label: osf_from_pin
nodes.subtitle: pin vs running version
nodes.summary: Reads .osf/version and compares it with the compiled package version; 'workspace' is always ok, a missing pin warns, a mismatch fails.

nodes.label: settings_check
nodes.subtitle: config::load
nodes.summary: Loads the config through the existing config module and reports where it came from, or the load error as a failure with a fix hint.

nodes.label: agents_check
nodes.subtitle: selection + credentials
nodes.summary: Resolves the agent selection, then for each enabled reviewer calls missing_credential to see whether an env var or login file satisfies it. Collects all missing credentials into one failure line.

nodes.label: missing_credential
nodes.subtitle: env_present + home
nodes.summary: Pure helper: given an agent, an env lookup closure and an optional home, returns the first missing-credential message or None. The closure keeps tests from mutating process-wide env.

nodes.label: hooks_from_status
nodes.subtitle: CheckStatus -> Check
nodes.summary: Maps each githooks::CheckStatus variant to a report line: installed is ok, not-set / retired / elsewhere all fail with the 'osf hooks install' fix.

nodes.label: container_check
nodes.subtitle: /opt/factory, /.dockerenv
nodes.summary: Probes two well-known paths to say whether the process is inside the factory image, in some other container, or outside one. Never fails — only ok or warn.

nodes.label: binaries_check
nodes.subtitle: always unknown
nodes.summary: A deliberate placeholder: agent binaries and pinned versions are reported as unknown until the launch templates land, so the gap is visible rather than silently passing.

nodes.label: osf lib
nodes.subtitle: pub mod doctor
nodes.summary: Registers the new doctor module so both the binary and the integration tests can reach it.

nodes.label: config
nodes.subtitle: config::load
nodes.summary: Existing settings loader; doctor calls it read-only to prove the config parses.

nodes.label: agents
nodes.subtitle: selection, Agent, AGENTS
nodes.summary: Existing agent registry and selection logic; doctor reads the enabled set, builder and reviewers from it.

nodes.label: githooks
nodes.subtitle: check, CheckStatus
nodes.summary: Existing git-hook inspector; doctor translates its CheckStatus into a report line.

nodes.label: reviewers::real_home
nodes.subtitle: now pub(crate)
nodes.summary: The only change to existing code: real_home is widened from private to pub(crate) so doctor can locate login files under the user's home.

nodes.label: git::repo_root
nodes.subtitle: root discovery
nodes.summary: Existing helper doctor uses to find the repository root, falling back to the current directory.

nodes.label: Repository files
nodes.subtitle: .osf/version, osf.toml, login files
nodes.summary: The on-disk inputs doctor reads: the version pin, the config file, and agent login files under the home directory.

nodes.label: Process environment
nodes.subtitle: credential env vars, HOME
nodes.summary: Environment variables doctor consults for agent credentials and for the home directory that anchors login-file lookups.

nodes.label: git config
nodes.subtitle: core.hooksPath
nodes.summary: The git setting the hooks check inspects, via the existing githooks module.

nodes.label: Container markers
nodes.subtitle: /opt/factory, /.dockerenv
nodes.summary: Filesystem markers that reveal whether the process runs inside the factory image or another container.

nodes.label: tests/doctor.rs
nodes.subtitle: integration tests
nodes.summary: Spawns the real binary to check the usage error for an unknown check, single-check filtering, JSON output shape, and a non-zero exit on a broken config.

views.title: osf doctor in the osf CLI
views.summary: The new subcommand sits on the CLI surface, builds a report from six small check functions, and leans on four existing modules plus the filesystem and environment for its inputs.
